# Diagrams

Use **Diagrams** beside **Board** and **List** to explore a project visually. You can create an empty diagram in the editor or generate one with a diagram action. Diagrams are saved as JSON files in the configured diagrams folder.

## Create a diagram

Select **New diagram**, then choose **Architecture**, **Dependency**, **Sequence**, **Flowchart**, **State diagram**, **Entity**, or **Mindmap**. mdÂ² saves an empty root diagram and opens it for editing. Flowchart and State diagram are two presets of the flow diagram type.

The **Add** menu offers objects appropriate to the chosen type. For example, an entity diagram offers entities and relationships; a sequence diagram offers participants, connections, and fragments. A mindmap starts with a root, then offers topics. Use **Select** to choose objects or **Pan** to move around the surface. The Diagram tab also has cut, copy, paste, delete, metadata, legend, and formatting controls.

To generate a diagram with an agent or command, run a project-level diagram action from the diagram view. The action must target a diagram context and declare diagram output. Its prompt or command receives an output path through {% raw %}`{{diagram-file}}`{% endraw %}. See [Action definition](../actions/action-definition.md) and [Placeholders](../actions/placeholders.md).

## Explore saved diagrams

Open a saved root diagram from the diagram view. Select an item to make it active. Use its context menu to run a child diagram action or open a saved child diagram. Breadcrumbs show the current path and let you return to a parent or choose another root diagram. The item menu also offers **Emphasize** to focus attention on an object.

## Edit and review

With a saved diagram open, choose **Edit diagram** on the **Diagram** tab. The editor shows **Current** (the source) and **New** (your editable version). On desktop, choose a vertical, horizontal, or tabbed comparison. On mobile, the comparison is tabbed. When you have just created an empty diagram, only **New** is shown.

Choose a tool from **Add** to place nodes, draw connections or groups, or add sequence fragments. Double-click a node, connection, or group to edit its details, or use the formatting controls. Moving, resizing, and changing diagram content appear in the change review; selection, pan, and zoom do not count as changes.

Select **Review** to see changes grouped by diagram, nodes, connections, groups, and fragments. Selecting a change highlights its affected objects. The review also shows generated change text and any validation problems. Resolve blocking items before using **Save** or **Send to agent**; both require at least one change.

**Save** writes an edited copy. The original diagram remains available, and later saves in the same edit session update that copy. **Send to agent** opens a diagram action with the reviewed change text, so the agent can implement the proposed changes. It does not save the editable diagram by itself.

## Diagram files and settings

Diagrams are structured JSON, not SVG images. The default folder is `design/diagrams` when the project folder uses its default `design`; change it with `project.diagramsFolder`. `project.diagramFooter` supplies the instructions appended to diagram action prompts and must include {% raw %}`{{diagram-file}}`{% endraw %}. See [Configuration](configuration.md) and [Project layout](../concepts/project-layout.md).

If none exists, reject Apply with a clear dialog error and make no changes. `Label` copies exact source label value to every compatible selected target.

Keep node and connection IDs, geometry, endpoints, group membership, and unselected objects unchanged. Record normal semantic changes and dispatch existing field- and legend-membership events only for changed values.

* Format Paste is enabled only with an active edit session, an eligible source, and at least one selected target of matching object kind. Node source changes selected nodes only; connection source changes selected connections only. Groups, opposite object kind, unselected nodes, and unselected connections remain unchanged.

* Applied changes render immediately through existing granular subscriptions, persist through normal diagram save flow, and remain available for semantic change review.
* Dialog is keyboard-operable, uses app theme, places actions bottom right, and reports failures through `dialogService`.

## Current state

* `AgentConversation.providerSessions` records the provider agent, conversation ID, synchronization point, timestamps, and usage baseline.
* `ActionAgentExecutor`, `agent_conversation.js`, and `agent_run_state.js` locate provider sessions by agent, so a conversation can hold only one effective session per provider.
* Switching agents for the first time starts a new provider conversation and sends the canonical MDÂ² conversation as context.
* Retry and compact flows assume the current agent's single global login owns the provider session.

## Implementation details

* Add optional `accountId` to each provider-session record. A missing value means that provider's initial account; do not rewrite or backfill existing conversation files.
* Treat a provider session's identity inside one `AgentConversation` as `(agent, resolved accountId)`. New and updated sessions persist the resolved account ID explicitly.
* When starting or continuing a conversation:
  * resume the provider session matching both the resolved agent and account;
  * if none exists, start a new provider conversation and send the complete canonical MDÂ² conversation as context, matching the current first-agent-switch behavior.
* Update provider-session normalization, persistence, synchronization, retry, and missing-session recovery to preserve account identity.
* Compaction must resolve and use the account stored on the selected provider session. Current desktop defaults and action/run overrides must not redirect an existing session.
* A retry of an existing turn remains on that turn's captured account. A fallback after a missing provider conversation may create a replacement provider session only for the same agent and account.

* Existing provider sessions without `accountId` continue under the corresponding initial account without file migration.
* Changing account defaults or names does not change the account used for an existing provider session.
* Retry and missing-session recovery keep the resolved account identity; removed references use the defined fallback.

ctrl tab in dashboard view should switch between topmost popup.

## Current state

* "Dashboard view" is the cards workspace view (`WorkspaceViewMode` `cards`, see J_63).
* Popup stack: `CardPopupService` (`app/src/services/card_popup_service.ts`) owns an ordered `entries` list of three kinds: `action` (rendered by `CardActionPopupHost`), `card-details` (`CardBodyPopover`), and `sequence` (`CardSequenceDialog`). The last entry is the topmost popup; `stackPosition` (list index) sets the z-index in `ResizablePopper`. In cards view every entry is visible; on mobile width only the top entry is visible.
* `activate(id)` moves one entry to the end of the list and dispatches `changed`. It does not move keyboard focus. Clicking or focusing a popup calls `activate` through `ResizablePopper` `onActivate` (`onPointerDownCapture`, `onFocusCapture`).
* Focus: `ResizablePopper` focuses its paper (`role="dialog"`, `tabIndex={-1}`) only once, on first mount (`focusOnMountRef`, `setPaperElement`). No way exists to focus an already mounted popup from outside.
* Keyboard: `KeyboardShortcutService` routes keys to the global service, then the active view service. `cardsKeyboardShortcutService` (`app/src/services/shortcuts/cards_keyboard_shortcut_service.ts`) is a stub that handles nothing. `TextKeyboardShortcutService` already maps Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab (`NEXT_LIST_TAB_SHORTCUT`, `PREVIOUS_LIST_TAB_SHORTCUT` in `list_tab_shortcuts.ts`) to next and previous open document.
* No popup component handles Ctrl+Tab itself, so the key reaches the window listener.

## implementation details

* Behavior: in cards view, Ctrl+Tab cycles forward through the popup stack: the bottom-most popup moves to the top. Ctrl+Shift+Tab cycles backward: the top popup moves to the bottom. Repeated presses visit every popup. After each cycle, keyboard focus moves into the new top popup.
* `CardPopupService`:
  * New method `cycle(offset: 1 | -1)`. With fewer than two entries, return `false`. Forward: move `entries[0]` to the end. Backward: move the last entry to the front. Call `setEntries`, then dispatch a focus request for the new top entry, then return `true`.
  * Focus request is a granular event per entry: type `focusRequested:<entryId>` (constant prefix in the module). Order matters: entries update first, focus request second.
  * New exported function `subscribeCardPopupFocusRequest(entryId, listener)` next to `subscribeCardPopups`; returns an unsubscribe function.
* `CardsKeyboardShortcutService`: replace the stub object with a class like `TextKeyboardShortcutService`, with dependency `{ popups: CardPopupService }`. `handleKeyDown`: on `NEXT_LIST_TAB_SHORTCUT` return `popups.cycle(1)`; on `PREVIOUS_LIST_TAB_SHORTCUT` return `popups.cycle(-1)`; else `false`. Singleton passes `cardPopupService`. Only call site: `viewServices` in `keyboard_shortcut_service.ts` (unchanged import name).
* `ResizablePopper`: new optional prop `subscribeFocusRequest?: (listener: () => void) => () => void`. An effect subscribes when the prop is set. On request: if `paperRef.current` exists, focus it; else set `focusOnMountRef.current = true`, so the paper focuses when it mounts (mobile: new top popup opens only after the reorder renders). Other `ResizablePopper` users (search panel, file search menu, diagram popups) pass nothing; unchanged.
* Pass the subscription from each card popup owner, built with `useCallback` on `entry.id`:
  * `CardActionPopupHostEntry` to `ActionPopup` (new optional prop), into `ActionPopupContentProps`, then `ActionPopupFrame` to `ResizablePopper`. Diagram action popups pass nothing.
  * `CardBodyPopoverEntry` to its `ResizablePopper`.
  * `CardSequenceDialog` to its `ResizablePopper` (only when `entry` exists).
* Focus side effect: focusing the new top paper fires `onFocusCapture`, which calls `activate` on the entry that is already top; no-op, no extra `changed` event.
* Edge cases:
  * Zero or one popup: `cycle` returns `false`; key is not handled; nothing changes.
  * Other views: text view keeps its Ctrl+Tab document switching; diagrams and stats views unchanged (cards service not active there).
  * Focus inside a text field of the old top popup: Ctrl+Tab still cycles; focus leaves the field.
  * Modal MUI dialog open above popups (delete card, affects editor): popups still reorder beneath; the dialog focus trap keeps focus in the dialog.
* Tests:
  * `card_popup_service.test.ts`: forward and backward cycle order with three entries; focus request fires for the new top entry only, after `changed`; fewer than two entries returns `false` and dispatches nothing.
  * New `cards_keyboard_shortcut_service.node.test.ts` (popup service stub): Ctrl+Tab calls `cycle(1)`, Ctrl+Shift+Tab calls `cycle(-1)`, return value passes through; other keys return `false`.
  * `resizable_popper.test.tsx`: focus request focuses a mounted paper; request while closed focuses the paper after open.
  * Run those files directly and `npm run lint` in `app/`.

## acceptance criteria

1. In cards view with two or more popups open (any mix of action, card details, sequence), Ctrl+Tab brings the bottom-most popup to the top.
2. Repeated Ctrl+Tab visits every open popup in turn and returns to the first after a full cycle.
3. Ctrl+Shift+Tab cycles in the opposite direction: the top popup moves to the bottom.
4. After each Ctrl+Tab or Ctrl+Shift+Tab, keyboard focus is inside the new top popup, also on mobile width where only the top popup shows.
5. With zero or one popup, Ctrl+Tab changes nothing.
6. Ctrl+Tab in text view still switches open documents; diagrams and stats views are unchanged.
7. Ctrl+Tab handling lives in `CardsKeyboardShortcutService` and `CardPopupService`; no shortcut registration in `.tsx` files.

When opening an action popup that contains a task list, but the list is completed, then collapse the task list by default.

## Current state

* `AgentTaskList` (`app/src/components/actions/conversation/tasks/agent_task_list.tsx`) renders the selected live or historical conversation's non-empty `taskList` inside `ActionConversationChat`.
* Header already shows completed and total task counts. Accordion uses `defaultExpanded`, so every task list starts expanded, including lists whose tasks are all completed.
* `ActionConversationChat` is the only `AgentTaskList` call site. Task-list updates already reach the component through its live-run and conversation-store subscriptions.

## Implementation details

* Define a **completed task list** as a non-empty list where every task has status `completed`.
* In `AgentTaskList`, set Accordion's initial expanded state from existing completed and total counts: start collapsed when both counts are equal; otherwise start expanded.
* Keep Accordion uncontrolled after its initial render. Completion while popup remains open must not force it closed, and user can expand or collapse it normally. Closing and reopening popup applies default again from current task statuses.
* Keep header progress count visible while collapsed. Do not change task data, live or historical subscriptions, action-popup layout, persistence, or desktop code.
* Update focused `AgentTaskList` tests. Verify completed lists start collapsed, incomplete lists start expanded, and manual toggling still works. Run affected test file and app lint during implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

* Opening action popup with non-empty task list whose every task is `completed` shows task rows collapsed by default.
* Opening popup with any `pending` or `inProgress` task shows task rows expanded by default.
* Collapsed header still shows `completed/total` count and remains accessible through existing `Toggle agent tasks` control.
* User can expand completed list and collapse or re-expand incomplete list.
* Task list becoming complete while popup is open does not override user's current expanded or collapsed choice. Reopening popup recalculates default from latest task statuses.
* Live and historical conversations behave same. Missing and empty task lists still render nothing.

# Stats

Stats connects agent activity to the cards, actions, and releases where the work happened. Use it to compare workflows, find expensive work, and export the displayed data for further analysis.

Select **Stats** beside **Board** and **List** in the application menu. The Stats workspace is available in the desktop app and on remotely connected devices.

## Choose what to measure

The **Dataset** control offers four views:

| Dataset | Questions it answers |
| --- | --- |
| **Activity over time** | How many cards and actions were completed? How many project tokens were used? |
| **Agent/model performance** | Which agents or models use the most measured time, tokens, or tool calls? |
| **Project usage vs account usage** | How does project work compare with Claude and Codex account-limit consumption? What is the estimated subscription cost? |
| **Totals by Card/Action** | Which cards or reusable actions account for the most time, tokens, or estimated cost? |

All datasets share the **Releases**, **From**, and **To** controls. Dates are entered in local time. Charts group values by UTC day, week, or month where the selected dataset supports that choice.

Select **Export CSV** to download the currently displayed dataset with its active filters. Exporting does not change the project's `usage_metrics.csv` file.

## Activity over time

Choose **Distinct cards**, **Completed actions**, or **Token usage**, then group the results by day, week, or month.

- A card is counted once in a time bucket when it has at least one completed action there.
- Completed actions count root actions, including actions whose main work completed but whose after-action failed.
- Token usage over time comes from timestamped provider turns in `usage_metrics.csv`.

Use this dataset to see delivery volume and activity trends. Use the other datasets when you need to compare agents, models, cards, or costs.

## Agent/model performance

Choose measured duration, tokens, or tool calls, then group by agent or model. You can narrow the chart to particular actions, agents, or models.

The available aggregations are:

- **Sum** â€” the combined value of the included action conversations.
- **Average** â€” the arithmetic mean per included action conversation.
- **Average Â± std dev** â€” the average plus a whisker showing one population standard deviation.
- **Median** â€” the middle value after the included conversations are sorted.

Measured duration counts time while an agent is running. Time spent waiting for user input is excluded. Completed, failed, and cancelled conversations can all contribute because each may consume time, tokens, and tool calls. The notice above the chart explains why any samples were excluded.

## Project usage vs account usage

This dataset aligns several day- or week-based charts:

- Account usage.
- Project token usage, as totals and as an average per completed action.
- Tokens per percent of account limit used.
- Tokens per dollar.
- Estimated cost per agent.
- Average cost per action.
- Actions per percent of account limit used.
- Project activity by agent and action.

Claude and Codex series keep distinct color families across these charts. Hover or focus a bar for its exact value and calculation context.

Account usage is account-wide. It may include other projects and direct CLI sessions, so these charts compare project work with account consumption; they do not prove that all account consumption came from this project.

Cost charts require a monthly subscription cost on the matching agent profile. See [Configure cost estimates](#configure-cost-estimates) and [How usage and cost are calculated](../concepts/usage-and-cost.md).

## Totals by card or action

Group by **Card** to find costly features and bugs, or by **Action** to compare reusable workflows. Choose measured duration, token usage, or estimated cost.

An estimated-cost total can include conversations from different agents. mdÂ² prices each supported conversation with its agent's calculated rate and labels the result **Mixed** when more than one agent contributed. The tooltip reports conversations that could not be priced instead of silently treating them as free.

## Select a release

Stats opens on **Current release**. The **Releases** control also lists each completed release discovered in the configured releases folder.

Release selection applies to activity, performance, card/action totals, and other activity-derived results. Timestamped project-token and account-usage rows cannot be assigned to a release, so they remain controlled by the date range only.

## Configure cost estimates

1. Open configuration with the gear button.
2. Open **Desktop** and edit the relevant agent profile.
3. Enter **Monthly subscription cost (USD)**.
4. Save the configuration.

The value must be greater than zero. It represents a monthly subscription price, not an API token price. mdÂ² combines it with observed account-limit consumption to estimate cost. If the price or usable account history is unavailable, token and time charts still work but the affected cost values remain unavailable.

## Missing or partial data

Stats is calculated from saved activity and `usage_metrics.csv`:

- Older conversations without a measured timer are omitted from duration results.
- Token usage over time is unavailable when `usage_metrics.csv` is missing.
- A newly configured subscription cost cannot price periods without usable account observations.
- Running and waiting conversations are not final performance samples.
- Invalid required activity data makes Stats unavailable instead of displaying misleading partial totals.

See [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md#stats-data-is-missing-or-unavailable) for common causes.

See also: [How usage and cost are calculated](../concepts/usage-and-cost.md), [Agent setup](../actions/agent-setup.md), [Board view](board-view.md).
